## IGST & Customs Readiness

> How IGST refunds, Shipping Bill errors and pre-LEO reconciliation actually behave on ICEGATE — and the readiness work that prevents blocked refunds.
> Hub: https://kananlabs.in/publications/cluster/igst-customs/

- [HS Classification Drift Across the Invoice, Shipping Bill and COO](https://kananlabs.in/publications/hs-classification-drift/): The same goods routinely carry different HS codes on the commercial invoice, the Shipping Bill and the Certificate of Origin, because each document is produced from a different master. The Shipping Bill demands the full eight-digit ITC(HS) item, RoDTEP rates diverge line by line at eight digits, and CAROTAR 2020 makes origin claims turn on classification-linked criteria.
- [e-SANCHIT: The Upload Failures That Stall Assessment and LEO](https://kananlabs.in/publications/e-sanchit-document-gaps/): e-SANCHIT is the only channel for supporting documents on ICEGATE, and it enforces a precise technical specification: PDF/A (ISO 19005-2), at least 200 dpi, 75 KB per A4 page within a 1 MB file, digitally signed with the DSC registered on ICEGATE. A defective upload yields no IRN, and without the IRN the document does not exist for assessment.
- [What One Documentation Failure Costs: Demurrage, Fees, Blocked Refunds](https://kananlabs.in/publications/export-documentation-failure-cost-anatomy/): A single documentation failure bills an exporter through four independent meters: container charges that escalate by slab at the terminal, bank discrepancy fees per presentation, fixed rectification fees at customs, and a refund clock that legally stops until the error is cured. The instruments are published — the anatomy is simply rarely added up.
- [SB005: Why Your IGST Refund Blocks After EGM and How to Clear It](https://kananlabs.in/publications/sb005-igst-refund-blocked/): An SB005 error blocks an IGST refund when the Shipping Bill invoice number diverges from the one filed in GSTR-1 Table 6A. The refund stalls silently after EGM; no rejection is issued. The fix is a Concordance Table (Annexure A) verified through the customs officer interface at ₹1,000 per Shipping Bill — the Shipping Bill itself cannot be amended.
- [Reconciling Invoice, Packing List, B/L and Shipping Bill Before LEO](https://kananlabs.in/publications/pre-leo-document-reconciliation/): Four documents describe one shipment — Commercial Invoice, Packing List, Bill of Lading and Shipping Bill — and customs, GST and manifest systems check them against each other after export, once Section 149 of the Customs Act has frozen the declaration. Pre-LEO reconciliation verifies identity, quantity, value and cargo fields for agreement while every record is still writable.
- [Invoice Number Formatting: How Tally and ICEGATE Disagree](https://kananlabs.in/publications/invoice-number-format-tally-icegate/): Rule 46(b) of the CGST Rules limits a tax invoice number to sixteen characters from letters, numerals, hyphen and slash. Accounting-software formats and the Shipping Bill entry routinely diverge — a dropped prefix, a slash swapped for a hyphen — and ICES matches invoice numbers exactly, so any divergence returns SB005 and stalls the IGST refund.
- [SB001–SB006: The ICEGATE Shipping Bill Error Codes, Explained](https://kananlabs.in/publications/icegate-sb-error-codes/): ICES validates every IGST export refund at invoice level against GSTR-1 data and returns one of seven codes, SB000 through SB006. Each error code names a specific mismatch — Shipping Bill details, EGM status, GSTIN or invoice number — and each has a fixing actor and procedure. Even SB000 does not always pay: four conditions gate the refund scroll.
- [RoDTEP 2026: The February Cut, the March Restoration, the Fine Print](https://kananlabs.in/publications/rodtep-2026-rate-volatility/): DGFT Notification 60/2025-26 cut all RoDTEP rates and value caps by 50% with effect from 23 February 2026. Notification 66/2025-26 restored the 22 February rates from 23 March 2026 — and its corrigendum confirmed the restoration is not retroactive, so exports with LEO between 23 February and 22 March 2026 (outside ITC HS Chapters 01–24) retain the halved rates.

## Marine Cargo Evidence

> Where marine cargo claims fail on evidence: time-bars, certificates, surveys — and the evidence packet that makes a claim defensible.
> Hub: https://kananlabs.in/publications/cluster/marine-evidence/

- [Subrogation Time-Bars: CGSA 2025's One Year, MTGA 1993's Nine Months](https://kananlabs.in/publications/subrogation-time-bars-cogsa-mtga/): India's cargo-claim clocks extinguish rights rather than merely bar remedies: suit against a sea carrier within one year of delivery under the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 2025, and against a multimodal transport operator within nine months under MTGA 1993. Once expired, the insurer's subrogation target is gone, and the cargo claim usually follows.
- [Open Cover vs Certificate of Insurance: Reconciling CIF+10%](https://kananlabs.in/publications/open-cover-coi-cif-plus-10/): An open cover insures only what is declared into it, and a Certificate of Insurance is only as good as its declared value. UCP 600 Article 28(f)(ii) sets the floor at 110% of CIF; Section 81 of the Marine Insurance Act 1963 makes the under-insured assured his own insurer for the shortfall; Section 64VB governs attachment.
- [Marine Cargo Claim Denial in India: A Taxonomy of Evidence Gaps](https://kananlabs.in/publications/marine-cargo-claim-denial-taxonomy/): Marine cargo claim denials in India cluster into four evidence families, not exotic perils: premium timing under Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938, policy exclusions such as ICC clause 4.3 on packing, procedural windows for notice and suit, and cross-document inconsistency across the invoice, packing list, B/L and Certificate of Insurance. Every family is checkable before sailing.

## EV & Lithium Export

> Export mechanics for EV and lithium-battery cargo: HS 8507 classification, dangerous-goods documentation, and the approvals that gate shipment.
> Hub: https://kananlabs.in/publications/cluster/ev-lithium/

- [EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542: The HS 8507.60 Compliance Calendar](https://kananlabs.in/publications/eu-battery-regulation-hs850760/): The EU Battery Regulation binds Indian HS 8507.60 exporters through their importers today — CE marking, declaration of conformity, technical documentation per Article 41 — while its headline obligations arrive on staggered dates: the battery passport on 18 February 2027, due diligence on 18 August 2027, and the EV carbon-footprint declaration only once its delegated act is finally adopted.
- [US Tariffs on Indian Exports 2026: From 50% to 10%, and the July Cliff](https://kananlabs.in/publications/us-tariffs-indian-exports-2026/): Between August 2025 and July 2026, the US tariff on Indian-origin goods moved from a stacked 50% to a 10% surcharge, through a trade framework, an Executive Order, and a Supreme Court ruling that voided the IEEPA tariffs. The Section 122 surcharge expires by statute on 24 July 2026; Section 232 duties on metals and autos stack separately and remain.
- [CBAM's Definitive Regime: What EU Buyers Now Ask Indian Suppliers](https://kananlabs.in/publications/cbam-definitive-indian-auto-components/): CBAM's definitive regime took effect on 1 January 2026. EU importers of covered iron, steel and aluminium goods above the new 50-tonne annual threshold must be authorised CBAM declarants, and their first declaration — due 30 September 2027 for 2026 imports — prices embedded emissions with certificates. The data burden lands upstream, on the Indian producer.

## Export Realization

> From Let Export Order to realized payment: e-BRC, RoDTEP, refunds, and the reconciliation between what was shipped and what was credited.
> Hub: https://kananlabs.in/publications/cluster/export-realization/

- [LC First Presentations: Why Seven in Ten Fail on Documents](https://kananlabs.in/publications/lc-first-presentation-discrepancies/): The ICC's own introduction to UCP 600 records that roughly 70% of letter-of-credit presentations were rejected on first presentation. The examination rules are mechanical: banks get five banking days, transport documents must be presented within 21 calendar days of shipment, the invoice description must correspond with the credit, and refusal comes as a single notice listing every discrepancy.
